body:
With `ZStarCoordinate` and a `SplitExplicitFreeSurface`, a tracer that starts at c ≡ 1 (and has value 1 at the boundary) doesn't stay at 1 next to open boundaries. In the interior it does, to round-off.

The cause is that σ and w̃ see different boundary transports. σ is advanced with η, and η is stepped with the substep `U`/`V` after the halo fill and transport pin. The filtered transport `Ũ`/`Ṽ`, which sets w̃ through ∂t σ = −∇·Ũ/H, disagrees with that at the boundary faces in two ways:

1. `Ũ`/`Ṽ` are accumulated in the velocity kernel, before the substep fill/pin. So face 1 gets pre-fill values, and face N+1 is outside the kernel range and never accumulated.
2. After substepping, `fill_halo_regions!((Ũ, Ṽ))` overwrites the boundary faces with the open-boundary value.

So (σⁿ⁺¹ − σⁿ)/Δt ≠ −∇·Ũ/H in the boundary rows only. Because the tracer update divides by σ, the result is a multiplicative error in every tracer there.

This PR:

- moves the `Ũ`/`Ṽ` accumulation into the free-surface kernel, using `U★` (the same transport that advances η);
- also accumulates face N+1 when the right side is `Closed`;
- builds `Ũ`/`Ṽ` with boundary conditions that drop `NormalFlow` sides, so the post-substep fill keeps the accumulated faces.

Fixing only (1) gives results bit-identical to main, because (2) overwrites the faces anyway.

In a small channel (`SplitRungeKutta3`, `GravityWaveRadiationBoundaryCondition` on both open sides, 200 steps), max |c − 1| goes from ~2e-5 on main to ~3e-15.
The new test in `split_explicit_boundaries.jl` runs c ≡ 1 under z★ through open north/south and west/east boundaries. It fails on main (|c − 1| ≈ 7e-6) and passes here (< 1e-12).

In a 16-day realistic regional run with open boundaries, the fix also removes the spurious bottom-cell jets that develop along the open boundaries without it.

This is a fix for `SplitRungeKutta3`. Under `QuasiAdamsBashforth2`, z★ doesn't keep c ≡ 1 even with closed walls (~4e-5 after 50 steps, identical on main and here). With open boundaries there is an extra boundary error of similar size (~1e-4), which this PR doesn't fix.

Related: #5812 changes the same kernel.

title: Keep uniform tracers uniform at open boundaries under z★ with split-explicit free surface

body:
## Problem

A bounds-preserving WENO scheme (`WENO(; bounds = (cᵐⁱⁿ, cᵐᵃˣ))`) combined with adaptive-implicit vertical advection (`time_discretization = AdaptiveVerticallyImplicitDiscretization(...)`) double-counts the vertical flux wherever the vertical Courant number `α = |w| Δt / Δz` exceeds `cfl`.

- With AIVA, the explicit vertical flux uses the CFL-limited velocity `w · min(1, cfl/α)` through `advective_tracer_flux_z(..., ::AVID, ...)`, and the implicit solve adds the remainder `w (1 - cfl/α)`.
- With `bounds`, `div_Uc` dispatches to `bounded_tracer_flux_divergence_z`, which builds its vertical fluxes from the **full** `w[i, j, k]` and never goes through `advective_tracer_flux_z`. The implicit part is still added because the scheme is still an `AdaptiveImplicitVerticalAdvection`.

So a bounded tracer is advected vertically by more than `w`. This is true even when the limiter is inactive (θ = 1), because the bounded code path is taken whenever `bounds` is set.

## How it showed up

In a global 1/6° tripolar hydrostatic run (z-star, `SplitRungeKutta3`, AIVA `cfl = 1`), salinity had `bounds = (0, 100)` and temperature had the same WENO without `bounds`. In a downwelling, nearly neutral coastal polynya column, salinity split within one step into a fresh top and a salty layer underneath. Column-integrated salt was conserved and T was unaffected. The salty layer sank, sped up the downwelling and ran away (S → 197, then negative, then a TEOS-10 `DomainError`). It failed sooner at longer Δt because more cells exceed `cfl`. Removing `bounds`, or this fix, removes it.

## Fix

In `bounded_tracer_flux_divergence_z`, scale `w` by `explicit_velocity_scaleᶜᶜᶠ` when the scheme's time discretization is `AdaptiveVerticallyImplicitDiscretization`, matching the unbounded path. Other time discretizations are unchanged. Horizontal bounded fluxes need no change, because AIVA keeps horizontal advection fully explicit.

Note that the limiter's bound guarantee assumes the explicit Courant number stays below `maximum_courant_number`. With AIVA's `cfl` above that value, the explicit part can still exceed it, so the strict bound is not guaranteed there. This PR only removes the double counting.

## Test

Added a test in `test/unit/bounds_preserving_advection.jl`: with a tracer far from its bounds and `α` up to 1.2 against `cfl = 0.5`, the bounded and unbounded schemes must give the same `div_Uc`.

- On `main`: max difference 126.6 (fails).
- With this PR: 1.1e-13.

body:
On `ReactantState`, a grid holds its coordinates as device arrays, and the plural node accessors are built on views of them. Reducing or broadcasting over those views reads the device arrays element by element on the host, which is a scalar-indexing error. Fixes #6325.

Some places this surfaces:
- `xnodes`/`ynodes` of a lat-lon grid, which broadcast `R * deg2rad(λ') * hack_cosd(φ)`. Every extent check on a regional lat-lon grid goes through them, for example `Relaxation`'s target-extent check while a nested model is built.
- `extrema(λnodes(…))`, as in NumericalEarth's bracket check and its `PrescribedAtmosphere` summary (NumericalEarth/NumericalEarth.jl#856, NumericalEarth/NumericalEarth.jl#858).
- `tidal_boundary_conditions`, which iterates `λnodes` and `φnodes` on the host.

All of these accessors reach their coordinate arrays through `Oceananigans.Grids._property`:
- `xnodes`, `ynodes`, `λnodes` and `φnodes` on a lat-lon grid;
- `xnodes` and `ynodes` on a stretched `RectilinearGrid`;
- `rnodes` and `znodes` on any grid;
- the two-dimensional form, on orthogonal spherical shell grids.

So the Reactant extension adds `_property` methods for concrete Reactant arrays. Each copies the coordinate array to the host once and returns the same interior view or halo-inclusive array as before, now on the host.

Inside a compiled function the arrays are traced, and inside a kernel the grid is adapted, so neither matches. In-kernel code and traced broadcasts are unchanged. The accessors are host conveniences, so a host array is the right return.

A Reactant unit test compares the accessors with the CPU grid's, at `Center` and `Face`, with and without halos:
- on a lat-lon grid: `xnodes`, `ynodes`, `λnodes`, `φnodes` and `znodes`;
- on a stretched `RectilinearGrid`: `xnodes`, `ynodes` and `znodes`.

body:
**This merges to**: `glw/thickness-weighted-coriolis`

it's a follow-up to #6450. As noted in https://github.com/CliMA/Oceananigans.jl/pull/6450#issuecomment-6702664746, the vorticity term of `VectorInvariant` momentum advection has the same partial-cell defect as the Coriolis term that #6450 fixes. This PR applies the same fix to both terms via one shared operator.

## Problem

`VectorInvariant(vorticity_scheme=EnergyConserving())` computes

    Fᵘ = - ℑy(ζ ℑx(Δx v)) / Δxᶠᶜᶜ,    Fᵛ = + ℑx(ζ ℑy(Δy u)) / Δyᶜᶠᶜ.

Weighted by `Vᵘ = Az Δzᶠᶜᶜ` and `Vᵛ = Az Δzᶜᶠᶜ`, the corner terms of its work are `ζ ℑy(Δy Δzᶠᶜᶜ u) ℑx(Δx v)` and `ζ ℑx(Δx Δzᶜᶠᶜ v) ℑy(Δy u)`. These cancel only when Δz is laterally uniform. With `PartialCellBottom` the term does net work, of the same size as `EnergyConserving` Coriolis.

## Change

* The corner-q flux of #6450 moves into `Operators` (`vorticity_flux_operators.jl`) as `vorticity_flux_xᶠᶜᶜ` and `vorticity_flux_yᶜᶠᶜ`. Each takes a corner vorticity `ω(i, j, k, grid, args...)`, either the relative vorticity `ζ` or the planetary vorticity `f`, and the flux uses `q = ω / h` with the active-face corner thickness `h` of #6450. The cancellation is corner by corner, for any `q` and any `h > 0`.
* `ThicknessWeightedEnergyConserving` now calls the operator with `fᶠᶠᵃ`. It is a two-line method, and the results are unchanged: all of #6450's tests pass, including the check against `EnergyConserving` for uniform Δz.
* On `PartialCellBottom` grids, `VectorInvariant(vorticity_scheme=EnergyConserving())` calls the operator with `ζ₃ᶠᶠᶜ`, so the total `(f + ζ)` term is energy-neutral. Every other grid keeps the existing code path.

The flux masks immersed faces only, as #6450's `masked_A*_q` did. An earlier attempt that also masked wall halos broke the check against `EnergyConserving` for uniform Δz at `Bounded` walls. That only affected the wall faces, which are not time-stepped.

## Results

The relative work `|Σ V (u Fᵘ + v Fᵛ)| / Σ V (|u Fᵘ| + |v Fᵛ|)` for random velocities. The grids are single-level `PartialCellBottom` grids over random depths from 8 m to 4000 m, with land:

| | vorticity term on `main` | vorticity term, this PR | `EnergyConserving` Coriolis | f + ζ, this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `RectilinearGrid`, periodic | 4.8e−2 | round-off | 3.4e−2 | round-off |
| `RectilinearGrid`, bounded | — | round-off | 2.3e−2 | round-off |
| `LatitudeLongitudeGrid` | 3.2e−2 | round-off | 9.0e−2 | round-off |

All flat-bottom grids are at round-off, before and after. The `main` column was measured on separate grids without land, and the bounded case was not run on `main`.

The time-stepping run is an unforced, inviscid single-level model over the same kind of grid, with `g = 9.81`, initial speed 1 m/s, `Δt = 60 s`, 20,000 steps (14 days) and `SplitRungeKutta3`:

| | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| linear free surface | blows up at step 4377 | bounded, E/E₀ = 0.50 to 0.58 |
| `ZStarCoordinate` | blows up at step 4256 | E/E₀ falls steadily to 0.44 |

On `main`, the per-step energy budget shows the vorticity work growing until the blow-up. With this PR it stays at about 1e−20.

### What this does not fix

The kinetic-energy gradient term `∇K` is not energy-neutral with a linear free surface, partial cells or not. Its work, `−Σ K ∇·(Aₕ u) = Σ K Az ∂tη`, is a kinetic-energy flux through the surface that nothing balances. That holds for the continuous linear-free-surface equations too. It causes the slow rise from 0.50 to 0.58 above, and it disappears with `ZStarCoordinate`.

With reduced gravity (`g = 0.01`) and 1 m/s, η exceeds the thin-cell thickness within about 20 steps, so the linear free surface stops being valid. In that regime both `main` and this PR blow up from the `∇K` term, and with `ZStarCoordinate` the thin columns drain. That is a regime problem, so the test below uses `g = 9.81`.

## Tests

In `test/coriolis/schemes.jl`:

* **Work test:** the `VectorInvariant` vorticity term is checked alongside Coriolis on the three partial-cell grids (rectilinear, lat-lon and stretched lat-lon), and must stay below `100 eps`. `relative_coriolis_work` is generalized to `relative_work`.
* **Growing mode:** a new testset adds `VectorInvariant(vorticity_scheme=EnergyConserving())` to the single-level model with `ThicknessWeightedEnergyConserving` Coriolis (`g = 9.81`, 2 m/s, `Δt = 30 s`, 4000 steps, under a second per run). It requires E/E₀ < 1 for both time steppers.

If the two new `PCBIBG` methods are removed, these 8 assertions fail. The work is 1e−2 to 7e−2, and E/E₀ reaches 2.9 and 3.3 even with `ThicknessWeightedEnergyConserving` Coriolis. With them, all 694 tests in the file pass.

Run locally on CPU with Julia 1.13: `coriolis/schemes.jl`, `unit/quality_assurance.jl` (explicit imports) and `hydrostatic_free_surface/immersed_boundaries.jl` all pass. I have not run the GPU tests, the doctests or the wider hydrostatic suites.
